stemMd: Which statement must be true in every permitted order?

options.label: A
options.textMd: Bronze must not be in position 2.

explanationMd:
Combine the ordering and placement constraints rather than assuming one example is unique. The statement "Glass must precede Bronze." holds in all 9 permitted orders. Generate the cases by placing any fixed-position item and adjacent block first, then discard arrangements that violate a remaining rule. For each alternative, an explicit permitted counterexample appears in its feedback.

Complete permitted orders (each arrow advances one position):
- Glass → Bronze → Wood → Clay → Stone
- Glass → Bronze → Wood → Stone → Clay
- Stone → Glass → Bronze → Wood → Clay
- Stone → Wood → Clay → Glass → Bronze
- Stone → Wood → Glass → Bronze → Clay
- Wood → Clay → Stone → Glass → Bronze
- Wood → Glass → Bronze → Clay → Stone
- Wood → Stone → Clay → Glass → Bronze
- Wood → Stone → Glass → Bronze → Clay

distractorRationale.a: A counterexample satisfying all the rules is Glass → Bronze → Wood → Clay → Stone. Thus this statement is not necessary.
distractorRationale.b: A counterexample satisfying all the rules is Glass → Bronze → Wood → Clay → Stone. Thus this statement is not necessary.
distractorRationale.d: A counterexample satisfying all the rules is Stone → Glass → Bronze → Wood → Clay. Thus this statement is not necessary.

Rules Glass must be immediately followed by Bronze. Wood must precede Clay. Bronze and Stone must not occupy consecutive positions. leave 9 valid orders: Glass>Bronze>Wood>Clay>Stone; Glass>Bronze>Wood>Stone>Clay; Stone>Glass>Bronze>Wood>Clay; Stone>Wood>Clay>Glass>Bronze; Stone>Wood>Glass>Bronze>Clay; Wood>Clay>Stone>Glass>Bronze; Wood>Glass>Bronze>Clay>Stone; Wood>Stone>Clay>Glass>Bronze; Wood>Stone>Glass>Bronze>Clay. Choice true counts: a=7, b=2, c=9, d=2; necessary requires all matches.
